sample_unit: medullary thyroid carcinoma cases with paired FNA and surgical resection

links.outcome: Agreement of AI digital Ki-67 index with manual counting on cytology specimens
links.effect: MCPI vs DCPI agreement fair (61%; kappa = 0.22); DCPI vs MSPI 67% (kappa = 0.33); digital vs surgical overall grade 56% (kappa = 0.11); digital analysis often overestimated Ki-67.
links.quote: Agreement between MCPI and DCPI was fair (61%; kappa = 0.22), with digital analysis frequently overestimating Ki-67 proliferation index.

links.outcome: AI performance when applied to cytology specimens, a new specimen context
links.effect: Overall grade agreement between digital cytology assessment and surgery was slight (56%; kappa = 0.11), indicating poor generalization to cytology specimens and need for specimen-specific validation.
links.quote: The limited performance of the AI-based digital quantification platform emphasizes the need for specimen-specific development and validation prior to clinical implementation.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of an AI-based digital quantification platform (DeepLIIF) against manual assessment for Ki-67 grading on cytology specimens, evaluating standalone diagnostic concordance without testing a deployment safeguard or practice.
